gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the only named hands-on test of a portable Level 2 charger that can run on a dryer outlet, Tom Moloughney's State of Charge test of the Grizzl-E Mini Connect 40A, scored it 104 ChargerRater points and a 5.0-star final after cold, heat, water-intrusion and truck-crush tests. That test ran on a NEMA 14-50 plug at the unit's 40 A rating, not on a 14-30 at 24 A.
standout_why: I compared against plugandrange.com/portable-chargers/nema-14-30, plugandrange.com/reviews/grizzl-e-mini and thechargecurve.com/home-ev-chargers/best-nema-14-30. Both Plug & Range pages say 'We have not bench-tested' and give only spec-sheet figures and their own arithmetic (24 A × 240 V = 5.76 kW). The Charge Curve says 'We do not run a testing lab'. It does cite EV Charging Stations' Grizzl-E Mini Connect review, but only for specs and UL listing, not for any test result. So a rival already points to the source without using its results. None of the 12 + 18 results ChatGPT got, and none of its cited NHTSA, Tesla or NeoCharge pages, has a named reviewer's figure for any of the candidates.
decides: This confirms the current pick rather than changing it. I found no named measurement at 24 A for the EVDANCE 14-30 or NACS units, the Splitvolt 24A, or the Tesla Mobile Connector with the 14-30 adapter, so no measured figure separates them. Price, the native plug and the connector still decide. The Grizzl-E Mini Connect is the only candidate with named abuse-test results. It could be added as the 'independently tested' option for buyers who may add a 14-50 later, with a clear note that it ships set to 40 A, must be turned down to 24 A or less, and was tested on a 14-50.
candidates: Tesla Mobile Connector + Gen 2 NEMA 14-30 adapter

findings.label: State of Charge ChargerRater score
findings.value: 104 ChargerRater points (5.2 stars), Tom Moloughney's own score 4.8 stars, final average 5.0 stars
findings.source_title: Grizzl-E Mini Connect Amazes in State of Charge EV Charger Review (EVChargingStations.com, Mark Kane, published 2024-11-09, updated 2024-12-17)
findings.note: Tested by Tom Moloughney (State of Charge) with a NEMA 14-50 input plug and a J1772 connector, at its 9.6 kW / 40 A rating. Current is adjustable from 7 to 40 A, so it can be set to 24 A for a 14-30, but the review did not test that setting. Moloughney: 'This is a fantastic unit at a great price.'

findings.label: State of Charge abuse tests
findings.value: Passed all five: cable still easy to handle after almost 40 hours in a freezer; charged after heating under a heat lamp; automatic restart; water intrusion; run over by a Ford F-150 Lightning
findings.source_title: Grizzl-E Mini Connect Amazes in State of Charge EV Charger Review (EVChargingStations.com)
findings.note: Pass/fail results. The article gives no freezer or heat-lamp temperature and no measured amps or kW. The 'almost 40 hours' freezer time is the article's own figure.

findings.label: InsideEVs abuse tests and score
findings.value: Stayed submerged for more than 30 minutes and passed; driven over by a Ford F-150 Lightning and a Rivian R1T and still 'worked perfectly'; final score 4.4 of 5 stars
findings.source_title: J+ Booster 2 EV Charger Review (InsideEVs, Tom Moloughney, 2022-11-25)
findings.note: This is a 40 A unit tested with its NEMA 14-50 and 5-15 adapters. The review does not cover a 14-30 adapter or the current it would set, and its cold test is scored only as 'average'. Its price in the review, $699.97 list ($559.98 Black Friday 2022), is out of date and not a current price.

findings.label: InsideEVs drop test
findings.value: Dropped 10 times from about 5 ft (1.5 m) onto concrete
findings.source_title: EV Charger Review: The AmazingE and AmazingE Fast (InsideEVs, Tom Moloughney, 2021-06-15)
findings.note: This is the only named review I found of a charger sold with a native 14-30 plug. It reports no measured amps or kW; 16 A / 3.8 kW is the spec. EVChargingStations.com's AmazingE review page (https://evchargingstations.com/chargerreviews/amazinge/, read 2026-11-17) now says 'These models are no longer being produced, so we've removed their reviews', so do not list it as a buyable pick.

unsourced: Measured amps or kW at the car for the EVDANCE 24A 14-30 or 10-30 (J1772 or NACS) from a named reviewer or lab. I searched State of Charge, EVChargingStations.com, InsideEVs and general reviews; I found only sponsored videos and affiliate roundups with no measurement method.

Any named review or measurement of the Splitvolt 24A portable charger. InsideEVs reviewed only the Splitvolt Splitter Switch, and the only measured figure (5.3–5.4 kW on a Kia Niro EV) is an anonymous buyer report I saw only in a search snippet.

A named measurement of the Tesla Mobile Connector on the Gen 2 14-30 adapter (kW at the car, efficiency or plug temperature). The 24 A / 5.7 kW rating appears in Tesla's Gen 2 Mobile Connector owner's manual, which I did not open, so it is not used here.

Plug or receptacle temperature at 24 A continuous on a NEMA 14-30, measured with a thermal camera by any named tester. I found none. Tom Moloughney's melted-outlet article (EVChargingStations.com, 2024-12-14) covers a 14-50 and gives only a 75 in-lb screw torque, with no temperatures.
Measured results from Car and Driver, MotorTrend, Consumer Reports or Wirecutter for any of the candidates. A search returned only unverified 'tested' affiliate sites.
